newsitem.title: USA: PSA takes aim at LA Cty decision on yield burning.
newsitem.headline: PSA takes aim at LA Cty decision on yield burning.

text.p: PSA The Bond Market Trade Association on Thursday challenged a decision by Los Angeles County lawyers not to hand over background data on a controversial "yield burning" study commissioned by the county.
The Los Angeles Metropolitan Transportation Authority charged in the 43-page study in December that Wall Street firms made roughly $1 billion in illegal profits from yield burning overcharges.

PSA recently said that the study is deeply flawed and asked lawyers representing the county, Washington, D.C-based Phillips & Cohen, on February 10 to supply the transaction-by-transaction data used by the study's authors to reach their conclusions. PSA also said the data needs to be submitted to other academics for independent review.
Phillips & Cohen rejected the request in a March 19 letter to PSA, which the law firm released on Thursday.
The firm said it has submitted background data to the Internal Revenue Service and to enforcement staff at the Securities and Exchange Commission, where it will get rigorous independent review.
But Ruth said on Thursday that Phillips & Cohen was reneging on a recent pledge.
Law firm partner John Phillips said in a Reuters Financial Television interview on February 13 that the study has "been submitted for academic review," including "peer review."
Ruth said Thursday, "We are sorry that he appears to have changed his mind."
"Clearly, submission to the IRS and SEC is not a substitute for rigourous analytical review by academic peers," she said.
"It is virtually unheard of in academic circles to refuse peer review," she said. "It further calls into question the credibility of the study."
